sourcedFrom: Beretta B22 Jaguar User Manual — UD6A0672 rev 1 (form code printed in the running header) (UNDATED — Beretta prints a form code rather than a year)
cleanIntro: The B22 Jaguar is a .22 that comes apart into upper and grip frame like a modern centrefire, and it has two rules that are entirely its own: it will not strip COCKED, and once the upper is off you must never let the hammer fall. Both will damage the fire control unit rather than merely annoy you.

steps.title: Unloaded first, chamber checked
steps.action: Magazine out and the chamber checked empty before anything else. A rimfire is not a lesser gun for this purpose — it will fire a round it was left holding just as readily.
steps.quote: MAKE SURE THE PISTOL IS UNLOADED. IF NOT, UNLOAD THE PISTOL. FOR MORE INFORMTION SEE “UNLOADING THE PISTOL AND CHAMBER” PAGE 15.
steps.cite: Beretta B22 Jaguar User Manual — UD6A0672 rev 1 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.18-19

steps.title: ⛔ Uncock it FIRST — and pull the bolt back as you do
steps.action: The B22 cannot be field stripped cocked. To uncock it without hurting the firing mechanism, pull the bolt back SLIGHTLY and then pull the trigger to drop the hammer. Dropping a cocked hammer on a closed action to "save time" is what damages the fire control unit.
steps.quote: The B22 Jaguar can not be field disassembled if the pistol is cocked. To prevent damage to the firing mechanism while uncocking the pistol, slightly pull back on the bolt before pulling the trigger to drop the hammer.
steps.cite: Beretta B22 Jaguar User Manual — UD6A0672 rev 1 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.18-19

steps.title: Magazine, then the compensator and its O-ring
steps.action: Press the magazine release and take the magazine out, then unscrew the compensator and take the compensator O-ring off the barrel. The O-ring is small, black and easy to lose on a bench — put it somewhere.
steps.aside: Remove the magazine by pressing the magazine release (catch) (1).
steps.quote: Remove the compensator (2) and compensator O- ring from the barrel.
steps.cite: Beretta B22 Jaguar User Manual — UD6A0672 rev 1 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.18-19

steps.title: Takedown button DOWN and HELD, upper forward
steps.action: Slide the upper receiver takedown button all the way down and KEEP it there while you pull the upper receiver assembly forward off the grip frame. Releasing the button mid-pull is what makes it feel jammed.
steps.aside: Pull the upper receiver assembly forward to separate it from the grip frame.
steps.quote: Slide the upper receiver takedown button (3) completely downward and hold it in the downward position during the following step.
steps.cite: Beretta B22 Jaguar User Manual — UD6A0672 rev 1 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.18-19

steps.title: ⛔ Upper is off — now NEVER let the hammer fall
steps.action: With the upper off the lower, do not manually cock the hammer and do not pull the trigger. There is nothing for the hammer to strike but the fire control unit itself, and Beretta says plainly that doing it will damage the pistol and the FCU. This is the single most expensive mistake available on this gun.
steps.quote: WHEN THE UPPER RECEIVER IS REMOVED FROM LOWER RECEIVER, THE USER SHOULD NEVER MANUALLY COCK THE HAMMER OR PULL THE TRIGGER AND ALLOW THE HAMMER TO FALL.
steps.cite: Beretta B22 Jaguar User Manual — UD6A0672 rev 1 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.18-19

steps.title: Barrel from the chamber end, then oil the feed ramp
steps.action: Bore solvent and a brush ALWAYS beginning at the chamber end, then dry patches, repeating until it is clean. Wipe the barrel exterior and the feed ramp with a solvent patch, let it dry, and put lubrication on the feed ramp — a dry ramp on a .22 is a feed stoppage waiting to happen.
steps.aside: Wipe down exterior of barrel and feed ramp with a solvent soaked patch.
steps.quote: Clean the barrel with bore solvent and a brush and then dry it with cleaning patches. Always begin at the chamber end. Repeat until the barrel is clean.
steps.cite: Beretta B22 Jaguar User Manual — UD6A0672 rev 1 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.23

steps.title: Recoil spring and guide, lightly
steps.action: Light oil on the recoil spring and its guide. After prolonged use it may need cleaning with gun oil and a brush first — a rimfire deposits far more unburnt residue than a centrefire, and the spring is where it collects.
steps.quote: Lightly oil the recoil spring and spring guide with gun oil. After prolonged use, it may be
steps.cite: Beretta B22 Jaguar User Manual — UD6A0672 rev 1 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.23

deepSteps.title: Upper receiver strip — turn it over and start with the recoil pin
deepSteps.action: With the upper off the grip frame, turn it over to expose the underside and take the recoil pin out. ⛔ Note which way round the pin sits before it moves — Beretta prints that instruction because the pin goes back either way and only one is right.
deepSteps.aside: Once the upper receiver is separated from the grip frame, turn the upper receiver over to expose its underside.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the recoil pin from the upper receiver. NOTE: To aid in the assembly, note the orientation of the recoil pin during disassembly.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta B22 Jaguar User Manual — UD6A0672 rev 1 (form code printed in the running header) — Upper Receiver Disassembly, printed p.19

deepSteps.title: Bolt out, then the barrel stud a quarter turn
deepSteps.action: Slide the bolt out of the upper receiver. Then rotate the barrel stud a QUARTER turn and take it out, and remove the set screw with a 3/32" hex wrench. The stud is a quarter turn — not a screw to be run out.
deepSteps.aside: Slide the bolt out of the upper receiver.
deepSteps.quote: Rotate the barrel stud (1) 1/4 turn and remove it from the upper receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta B22 Jaguar User Manual — UD6A0672 rev 1 (form code printed in the running header) — Upper Receiver Disassembly, printed p.19

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Ejector clips are handed — note which one you have
deepSteps.action: Left-hand and right-hand ejector clips are DIFFERENT parts. Note the orientation before you touch it, then compress it with a flathead screwdriver or a pick from behind and lift it out. Fitting the wrong one back, or the right one backwards, gives you a gun that will not eject.
deepSteps.aside: Use a flathead screwdriver or pick behind the ejector clip to compress and remove the ejector clip.
deepSteps.quote: Note the orientation of the ejector clip (3), left and right-hand ejector clips are different.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta B22 Jaguar User Manual — UD6A0672 rev 1 (form code printed in the running header) — Upper Receiver Disassembly, printed p.19

deepSteps.title: Barrel out — and note which way it sits
deepSteps.action: Take the barrel out of the upper receiver, noting its orientation as the book's figure shows it. Going back, the barrel rib aligns to the groove on the FCU and the upper receiver tabs to the catch — that alignment is what lets the upper click home.
deepSteps.aside: When assembling the gun, align the the barrel rib (1) to the groove on the FCU (2) and the upper receiver tabs (3) with the catch (4).
deepSteps.quote: Remove the barrel from the upper receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta B22 Jaguar User Manual — UD6A0672 rev 1 (form code printed in the running header) — Upper Receiver Disassembly, printed p.19

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Springs are a wear item — 7,000 rounds
deepSteps.action: Beretta publishes a replacement interval for two springs on this pistol: the trigger return spring and the recoil guide spring, both at 7,000 rounds or sooner if malfunctions appear. Note the round count somewhere; a .22 gets there faster than anything else you own.
deepSteps.aside: The firearm should not be disassembled for cleaning beyond what is described. Only gunsmiths or other highly-trained personnel who are familiar with these firearms should conduct further disassembly.
deepSteps.quote: 7,000 Rounds or sooner if malfunctions occur
deepSteps.cite: Beretta B22 Jaguar User Manual — UD6A0672 rev 1 (form code printed in the running header) — Recommended Spring Maintenance, printed p.23

cleaning.name: BARREL & FEED RAMP
tasks: Solvent and brush from the CHAMBER end, dry patches until clean
Barrel exterior and feed ramp wiped with a solvent patch
⛔ Feed ramp LUBRICATED after it dries — a dry ramp jams a .22

cleaning.name: BOLT & UPPER
tasks: Rimfire residue off the bolt face and the extractor
Grooves of the upper wiped out

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING & GUIDE
tasks: Lightly oiled; cleaned with gun oil and a brush after prolonged use
⛔ Replace at 7,000 rounds, or sooner if it starts malfunctioning

cleaning.name: GRIP FRAME & MAGAZINES
tasks: Residue off the frame and out of the magazine well
Magazines cleaned; ⛔ never spray or apply oil to cartridges

reassembly: Barrel back into the upper the way it came out, ejector clip in its correct hand and orientation.
Set screw and barrel stud back in, the stud turned 90 degrees as the figure shows.
Bolt into the upper, recoil pin back in ITS ORIGINAL ORIENTATION.
⛔ Align the barrel rib to the groove on the FCU and the upper receiver tabs to the catch, then hold the grip frame and push the upper BACKWARDS until it clicks.
Compensator O-ring and compensator back on the barrel.
Function check with an empty magazine before any ammunition.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: verify the safety is ENGAGED, insert an EMPTY magazine and retract the bolt so it stays open, then pull it back and release it to close. Confirm the upper clicked fully into place on the grip frame — if it did not, the barrel rib is not in the FCU groove and it must come apart again rather than be forced.
